9700C2E0DFE501316DC168A86D17958E.description: Apply grades 11—12 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning [e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court Case majority opinions and dissents] and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy [e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses]").

97006A10DFE501316DC068A86D17958E.description: Apply grades 11—12 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics").

97000460DFE501316DBF68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

96FFAB10DFE501316DBE68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and over-reliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation.

96FF5280DFE501316DBD68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

96FF0390DFE501316DBC68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

96FEAEE0DFE501316DBB68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

96FE4850DFE501316DBA68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

96FDEF50DFE501316DB968A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

96FD52D0DFE501316DB768A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

96FCEF90DFE501316DB668A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

96FC6860DFE501316DB568A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).

96FC11B0DFE501316DB468A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

96FBBA10DFE501316DB368A86D17958E.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

96FB4910DFE501316DB268A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

96FAD720DFE501316DB168A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

96FA8780DFE501316DB068A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

96FA3830DFE501316DAF68A86D17958E.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

96F9E9C0DFE501316DAE68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

96F999A0DFE501316DAD68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

96F94590DFE501316DAC68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

96F8ED30DFE501316DAB68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

96F89C50DFE501316DAA68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

96F83D80DFE501316DA968A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

4FE027B979ED4BEBBEFC5ADECAAD8790.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile and analogy to manage the complexity of the argument.

96F7E180DFE501316DA868A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

96F787E0DFE501316DA768A86D17958E.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

96F71490DFE501316DA668A86D17958E.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

96F692C0DFE501316DA568A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

96F595B0DFE501316DA268A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

96F4F7E0DFE501316DA068A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

96F4A6A0DFE501316D9F68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

96F45440DFE501316D9E68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

96F40170DFE501316D9D68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

96F3A680DFE501316D9C68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

96F34A50DFE501316D9B68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

96F2EB50DFE501316D9A68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

96F23D20DFE501316D9868A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

96F1E3C0DFE501316D9768A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

96F19610DFE501316D9668A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

96F0EAC0DFE501316D9468A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

96F096E0DFE501316D9368A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

96F041A0DFE501316D9268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

96EFDAA0DFE501316D9168A86D17958E.description: Synthesize information from a range of sources (e.g., texts, experiments, simulations) into a coherent understanding of a process, phenomenon, or concept, resolving conflicting information when possible.

96EF7B00DFE501316D9068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the hypotheses, data, analysis, and conclusions in a science or technical text, verifying the data when possible and corroborating or challenging conclusions with other sources of information.

96EF29C0DFE501316D8F68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., quantitative data, video, multimedia) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

96EE8150DFE501316D8D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text, identifying important issues that remain unresolved.

96EE1BF0DFE501316D8C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the text structures information or ideas into categories or hierarchies, demonstrating understanding of the information or ideas.

96EDBDE0DFE501316D8B68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 11—12 texts and topics.

96ED12F0DFE501316D8968A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a complex multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks; analyze the specific results based on explanations in the text.

96ECAB40DFE501316D8868A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; summarize complex concepts, processes, or information presented in a text by paraphrasing them in simpler but still accurate terms.

96EC43C0DFE501316D8768A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts, attending to important distinctions the author makes and to any gaps or inconsistencies in the account.

96EB9580DFE501316D8568A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

96EB3C80DFE501316D8468A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

96EAEBB0DFE501316D8368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

96EA9330DFE501316D8268A86D17958E.description: Integrate information from diverse sources, both primary and secondary, into a coherent understanding of an idea or event, noting discrepancies among sources.

96EA42F0DFE501316D8168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate an author's premises, claims, and evidence by corroborating or challenging them with other information.

96E9EAB0DFE501316D8068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, as well as in words) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

96E923B0DFE501316D7E68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate authors' differing points of view on the same historical event or issue by assessing the authors' claims, reasoning, and evidence.

96E8A640DFE501316D7D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail how a complex primary source is structured, including how key sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text contribute to the whole.

96E83720DFE501316D7C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including analyzing how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

96E798E0DFE501316D7A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate various explanations for actions or events and determine which explanation best accords with textual evidence, acknowledging where the text leaves matters uncertain.

96E74280DFE501316D7968A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary that makes clear the relationships among the key details and ideas.

96E6D6D0DFE501316D7868A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, connecting insights gained from specific details to an understanding of the text as a whole.

96E62520DFE501316D7668A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

96E5C2E0DFE501316D7568A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

96E552B0DFE501316D7468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

96E4E800DFE501316D7368A86D17958E.description: Analyze seventeenth-, eighteenth-, and nineteenth-century foundational U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (including The Declaration of Independence, the Preamble to the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, and Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address) and other documents of similar significance for their themes, purposes, and rhetorical features.

96E49C30DFE501316D7268A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. and other texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning (e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court majority opinions and dissents) and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy (e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses).

96E44F90DFE501316D7168A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively) as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

96E3ABA0DFE501316D6F68A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness, or beauty of the text.

96E345B0DFE501316D6E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

96E2EC50DFE501316D6D68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

96E23090DFE501316D6B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.

96E1D040DFE501316D6A68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the text.

96E14DF0DFE501316D6968A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

96E03F20DFE501316D6668A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

96DFCC10DFE501316D6568A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

96DF5240DFE501316D6468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature and other literary canons, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics.

96DF0660DFE501316D6368A86D17958E.description: Analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text. (Include at least one play by Shakespeare and one play by an American dramatist.)

96DE2060DFE501316D6068A86D17958E.description: Analyze a case in which grasping point of view requires distinguishing what is directly stated in a text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

96DDCD40DFE501316D5F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

96DD7530DFE501316D5E68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or powerful language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (Include Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

96DCD6A0DFE501316D5C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, how the characters are introduced and developed).

96DC7100DFE501316D5B68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the text.

96DBFCD0DFE501316D5A68A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

96DAFAB0DFE501316D5768A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

96DAAA70DFE501316D5668A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

96DA4D00DFE501316D5568A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

96D9E890DFE501316D5468A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

96D998C0DFE501316D5368A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

96D90430DFE501316D5168A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

96D8B760DFE501316D5068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

96D86400DFE501316D4F68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

96D7AF80DFE501316D4D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

96D762B0DFE501316D4C68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

96D71570DFE501316D4B68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

96D66390DFE501316D4968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: ID Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

94ECBF50DFE50131696E68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

94EC5EE0DFE50131696D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

94EC1630DFE50131696C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

94EBCA90DFE50131696B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

94EB70D0DFE50131696A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

94EAE8E0DFE50131696968A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

94EA9A10DFE50131696868A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).

94EA5140DFE50131696768A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

94EA0630DFE50131696668A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

94E962A0DFE50131696468A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

94E8D0E0DFE50131696268A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

94E880E0DFE50131696168A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

94E7B2A0DFE50131695F68A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

94E76050DFE50131695E68A86D17958E.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

94E718C0DFE50131695D68A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

94E680D0DFE50131695B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

94E62D20DFE50131695A68A86D17958E.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, two; there, their).

94E5DF70DFE50131695968A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

94E54100DFE50131695768A86D17958E.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

94E4F670DFE50131695668A86D17958E.description: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

94E4A7F0DFE50131695568A86D17958E.description: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

94E44E40DFE50131695468A86D17958E.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

94E40510DFE50131695368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

94E324F0DFE50131695068A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

94E2D2B0DFE50131694F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

94E269F0DFE50131694E68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

94E1C960DFE50131694C68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

94E13390DFE50131694A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

94E0E470DFE50131694968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

94E01DF0DFE50131694768A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

94DFA670DFE50131694668A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

94DF5400DFE50131694568A86D17958E.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

94DF0120DFE50131694468A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

94DE5A00DFE50131694268A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

94DE0C10DFE50131694168A86D17958E.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

94DDC490DFE50131694068A86D17958E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

A88A0B149D76481A9F4BFCA494618C6E.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

770092A389E146AB9324121BEB23819D.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

C72CF6C7196C49928B7C43D0CF4E02D0.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

08742281137D4534A55E3A6097F6EC79.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

79AD94DC6E5F4FF69E38E96F22744037.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

62F9995F617D4A97A31C2968C6803F06.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

01379959C79C42098778B4801CCF283D.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

EB8B8084ABAA4B95921955DE1EE523B9.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

459FC7D0E2D34DFD94696700583BADC3.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

CBAD5F25D5894F40B24F8B7721852EE3.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

0934A3EF1FD54E5E991946905BA9F238.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.

C75944AD5986406085DEFBBD1EE4C246.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.

482FAD7600A64ED8B868D9AC9DB8A6D9.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

C1688B6DF24C461780F2F9D98B0BDFFF.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two- column table.

0DA3F0505E274EEA911317D1169C4BE1.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

43A16919810849F484FDFAB768263D8F.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

E5A607DE197C45C2984449C86F397355.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

96DC3026F17147BCA98EC798B5A4D605.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.

96DB29A3C5D74743BA93AA73FFC31141.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

960B97F0CF5D45ECA2A40C22F9B2D355.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

305840BD6340472E8BA22D42D341358E.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

E80DD452F6C84DDB81B576126F1EFB3C.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.

5F6DCBD5155C41B7B1A9AD7B2ABBC9A5.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

B3EAB179DC154D2B9E6154BADB60AE8D.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

5C86A40CA51449B8842C4D4D799F3340.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

1F0C832E37EF40FFA7A8BE09DDE17A0B.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

75A1E7E813A540FAB78E08D6702DD42E.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

C21686C6B01642C2B542989B63B0591D.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

D16EAAABF5B24413B0C4C24D52318EAF.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

1DE6F9E6B1C54C0E88037B3A2F88F75A.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

F8ABA6FE3F6246BB8098D418CD7376D2.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

D6A3870DFDEE4868AA8AE23BC0AA9874.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

EDFC3FB15ADE416BB871FD9236E59420.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

A938FF9E076544509798FFD5E1FB0C00.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

B0E76A1D60E942969F0898AB799E6AEB.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

F84F9407A52844E4BA67F24E672D389E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

D0073C8646BA441ABF28307F13F34DE0.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

A821ED0A29CD4FC7BE23077F6BFA57A1.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

BB77B5C506F343D188427610DAA9C8F1.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

6FA7D79AE078477A810EFF69C230900C.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

97F2E40E58864C759E67D61D34C0F928.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

B4E31F58096241D9902CD79BB5980667.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.

5580255481C4437B8E2A71C3E234597E.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is prime or composite.

588F8EE76D454F7E92C5901FA83629FB.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

87A0C5A327244D2A869CE5285BEDE36C.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

17F830DDCA454B9599A3D8F2F3E8ACC3.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

E1BA77508A8B4991BCFA06CD9D320675.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

9D855DDD92374FB7B0D317C5C464CCE8.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

BF6F4C45DCAA425AAE4869A7A5CBA569.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

839AE956A554409197D71617D517ADE3.description: Look for and make use of structure.

A1C37213B3C74FB09CF8C4DED1482834.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

7764E0510878474D9C44FE74ABF62916.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

763BBA15E3984FDFA605F24C548D50BC.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

B82A79E18DE9411E9424901F854C4A6C.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.

420A4A8899DE43A7A7089AC9B08A5D82.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

62237D5CAB89437E986D0C87B02BCEB7.description: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

E76729253852444FB8CCD1AE774D21F6.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

20D579786B734EE8B31D3C9C30D3C5FB.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

710B5E510A2B461B976705A837DE5E25.description: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

EAB42B0BB024465BADFC0FE347DD62CC.description: Apply the formulas V = l × w × h and V = b × h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole- number edge lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems.

DAFBF2825A3C4024A1E734282F4E5F14.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.

8231D37A58644DB1AF315C8A7F86E798.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real world and mathematical problems involving volume.

C233F0C41F2A4EB78B0E66F6EF23F0AF.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.

ABB97BD16579450F8274FBD642B972EC.description: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

67079E7B2A834CFC8B73C1E4B54F0D1A.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

0553862AD6F94CDD9F31A691D77A5343.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

E5EF36D8C8F94E06BD11F1B32C0729CF.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

EBA0D29F50A04C08BB04E24BEAF74C01.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots.

A3A69312ECE847D9B216C79842F9C66D.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real world problems.

DCD599CAC5FE4F99B1A9E10FD0B3DEA7.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

532A30E74CB24E979B0EE3FC334ACAFB.description: Solve real world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

398BB3E84D7A4C8AAF6BDAA24B144EFB.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.

F1454CC0FFCE4636A2619391A8D1B17D.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.

7E4713A64224403A842BB59D7C6EF7EF.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.1

2E3008D3B7CE4DA4BE1B81522CA600F4.description: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

D145879E9B084A75A1911181DB6A1756.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n×a)/(n×b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.

65E4F6E3F7EF43CCA384DCA89ABA4442.description: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

55D5836310FF4BE58FE4A10869591BF1.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

58DF6C3A7CA04334BA6B7705F4F13081.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a part of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b.

474AFBA880C84FE9953D1225057AEF66.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

EC410807B9A2407E874B932896EF7AAD.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

6A1BA3F363054F8C84382C11834B375D.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

1C288C19C9E54C6E98BACA790AFDFD0C.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fraction to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.

2814DD759BE94F329072EF016FF587FB.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.

5AB4C7A315554F81AECB2710AF65A038.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

DBAA7E59535A4FA3A20CAFC7C73459A1.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

B92D6ABF064741BBA798B4C20ADC96F6.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

D9C68A64CFA345599E7610169A679268.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

6327EF0F1CF0418FBEE64A465D46739A.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

5CB2D00AEC78482FA389B98D4E6EF17D.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

BF4E2300B1F04EE0AC8AB2B14007B043.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

08D258A458CE4159A6EBC599064AC4C0.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., 347.392 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 7 × 1 + 3 × (1/10) + 9 × (1/100) + 2 × (1/1000).

DC50BA4D2782490DA43EABB685452385.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

2A6F5240519F49F4B806807408C0C0A6.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

153802D135844C86916EC08C554FD7CC.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

1AD73A50A36D4FAAAB0FC9D5C62CE22E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

CCA16983781C41909F211F192FAD48BA.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

7B5EA0924A8641A09B75C3CC895FD2BE.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.

ED84A42A97394215A1A3B0889FB51EDD.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

004B986890F446B28873C8309C7D7CA6.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

3A092DE4D40644FDA032E456DCD638E3.description: Look for and make use of structure.

6F37A469DD4244FE9C850CBC9F68A9AE.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

9BBE5522FBD24E5085CE7D2E1845C8CB.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

BAAB89AD13444BDB99EE0FEB007A0CD6.description: Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.

C2208BF59BF54A5F87157B3377654822.description: Giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (interquartile range and/or mean absolute deviation), as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data were gathered.

BE804B25BDAF481C965B5BE7DCB89905.description: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.

E2A3874F3FBA463E9AA634ECFD7B3E42.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, such as by:

C235F5A3AB5F4DF886571880EB0457D5.description: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.

788C462D6E1E4068AEB44298A47502D0.description: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number.

37FDF767B41E46C3A5BE5F27C47D9AA0.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

484B5C3CD3A943C68755BE1077409C56.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.

6EF6906480744DCC8631CC9B719375DB.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.

A47B45219DC54351AA6C2E7EA5300C2D.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

92A09A2A4BB54746B766C79731A7E8D2.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.

0E9918CE0FAF4A0A849C762110CFF740.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

BA7BA23224B9471F8D55B1627D97EDE6.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

3808147CBF20494990CBF6631FB0348F.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.

98932A4EE1D54C9AAAB34A0EA0F35B86.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

880FF92A210A421FA9F7CF29AA0FB572.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent (i.e., when the two expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them).

44F00C50C87449AEBF298C5A6D056705.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

496444A1192B42D1B4F63E1F9E34B5D9.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole- number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

6187E806F98B4775AAA0EB0FFE5B1F2A.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.

BBF187D0B5D34FEEB8559EAF33437760.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.

22BEDBF9703A46B781F35E260CC1825B.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

0FA974B58D7F464E80E9401235BE449A.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

B818298D7D6A4804906277D750A2804A.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

D7FCE493850141A2B9973C3A9F92019D.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

910C1BB5E9124F85A20E253CA8407AF8.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

78FDF2219E1745BE9E1C9AD7269BA5D4.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation.

9035E4B1F3A94DC390BA17C4374FD624.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.

92C3DFCCA8AD422EB0CA426F704523CC.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.

AC11E624C3294EB0B267536092CC5F1C.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

C35588DC5CBC49C0A9A4B7C19964BE40.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

226689EE68664C97997C5E3556DF9F25.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

C945DE495925495DA30C7EDA2787F74E.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, e.g., –(–3) = 3, and that 0 is its own opposite.

03022E721C0140D7BA6DE9D8953F3482.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.

95BF6EB40F8142048B314BCD72557E14.description: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, positive/negative electric charge); use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.

C8AF2BCD64744B8F84704362F4FBEA26.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

208100840DDB4072A5DCDB4A35CCC202.description: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1–100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor.

38D10C6862B74D239EC03C771D84354F.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.

697AD9199D72432CBDAFBD886C604B74.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

1B4CC2826E064486B058BFA9F06FD72E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 9-10 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

E45A640BC47141938BC0E8CE24643313.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook, Turabian's Manual for Writers) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

5673B5441341479EAE075300BF1280F4.description: Use a colon to introduce a list or quotation.

D62EDDEAB0544C1584DC31BDC0EBA9F1.description: Use a semicolon (and perhaps a conjunctive adverb) to link two or more closely related independent clauses.

2FF7A361AE9F4A5EAFC070EFFBCE752C.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

3026DEE678C446A38F79A6BADDEF5019.description: Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, participial, prepositional, absolute) and clauses (independent, dependent; noun, relative, adverbial) to convey specific meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

C415877FDE5B46F4A20041A8AC0F11B2.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source.

0EBA30762C004D879607EC106657DC21.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on- one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 9-10 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

E1CE19A4FECC4827A34DC29389BE3AD4.description: Apply grades 9-10 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work [e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare]").

8CC25C23D6774406843980096F4F7CF0.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

DE17A52BDB7C4DBE969DA66B743C3081.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

18338A251A554FB1AAB99EBE81AB3FB9.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

1E731D3AAD7D4311BD46F60A6997F16A.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

BE6AFCB80AB34CFFADFB7ED0ACBA5574.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

93AEA0F3D6E74D5D9CF9B732C54B6C64.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language standards 1-3 up to and including grades 9-10.)

4661A35B66B048D1A44D9885651A3487.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1-3 above.)

E20786AAD1604217B3592761E8498613.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

55694DF6512347A39877EECA33165BFE.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

873E1A1FA9444AAFB0657E7DBDE7CE51.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole.

E511DB3DE50F45DCB6F1B52EE3FBB0F7.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

A2294ADABFE94D7C80E0DF3B4EBFA003.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

E5491A191E104215BB01D7A1A86EDE6E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

F8CDC1E1E1344E52892BB44A6F86BB5E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

DF92140A8A364DB58AC085E2A3ABCD0B.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic.

99FA08D41DE14405B64B57F2A7826A95.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

717E4AAFE38843BDAB2C8D6882CF0BB9.description: Develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant, and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

A9C8DF97D4434B358A61D53D42C39BF0.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

D5FC917FC5284EA28899F60CEED93744.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

A37E1960642B43929BCA77C612485CBD.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

881C017AEF52426DACC277F363CADE2C.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

425DC0AD27614F9DBDFDE11909284599.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the argument.

C667E5C4B5D645C99D03CF01DA820256.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

E58C3C58AFFD4989A5C43B31E7DD94FE.description: Introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

29C3071CB7A34896A158C104BC2FAE7D.description: By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 9-10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range. 7ADDB04D2F7347CB9F60F74045D3843D.description: Analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or series of ideas or events, including the order in which the points are made, how they are introduced and developed, and the connections that are drawn between them.

209C00383E434DCE9B6941929558A9D3.description: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

D4B9C0AF46724A999FF231914444FBD1.description: By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 9-10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range. EBAC8E686C9541A3A95691728A28FE08.description: Analyze the representation of a subject or a key scene in two different artistic mediums, including what is emphasized or absent in each treatment (e.g., Auden's "Musée des Beaux Arts" and Breughel's Landscape with the Fall of Icarus).

5D8FFF0FDE8C4FCAB4043CC38602C861.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language evokes a sense of time and place; how it sets a formal or informal tone).

F7BBF5885C8E4C95A672C2B9AEEA389B.description: Analyze how complex characters (e.g., those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop over the course of a text, interact with other characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme.

7D0B91111F334C239761E7B8BB42E08F.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

75FD78FB0EED4510A747AA9DF9FB3AC9.description: Draw ample evidence from grade-level texts to support claims and inferences, attending to the precise details of the authors' descriptions or explanations through quoting, paraphrasing, and citing textual references.

8F36B1CF7AB6496CB638840773E442A7.description: Regularly engage in a volume of reading related to the topics and themes being studied to build knowledge and vocabulary. document.title: Idaho Content Standards English Language Arts/Literacy

52B9ADA11DB54158B2971133420EB965.description: Spell correctly, consulting reference materials to check as needed.

8E32603CB57641E686FA9C7559FE9E56.description: Reflect appropriate manuscript requirements in writing, including correct use of seriation (headings and subheadings).

5A9164D585DD474CB9A43083AB43DC97.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of English punctuation and capitalization when writing and reading aloud to create meaning.

8D1925D169EC4EE2ABB136CDF1F6B330.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English when appropriate to task and situation; and distinguish where informal discourse is more appropriate.

B1D623A90365421DB4B7D687B099BDFA.description: Vary syntax for effect, consulting references (e.g., Tufte's Artful Sentences) for guidance as needed.

44C2FCD7AB8044B593908781C884A49C.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook, Turabian's Manual for Writers) appropriate for the writing type.

CF1155AF44C84686B737360851B0909F.description: Use a variety of sentence structures, including compound and compound-complex sentences with effective coordination and subordination of ideas and parallel, repetitive, and analogous sentence structures.

783BE94ED1EC46FE9BD13998072234C8.description: Apply the understanding that usage is a matter of convention, can change over time, and is sometimes contested, consulting references (e.g., Merriam-Webster's Dictionary of English Usage, Garner's Modern American Usage) as needed.

1EECD01888D74A2B87FFF3FE2A0DB251.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D73AA1F525AA456A885D705AE685A381.description: Make strategic use of digital media in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

060323E35C974890AA314E25A71D3AB8.description: Analyze multiple interpretations of a text (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text.

19092D786141441AAF9577A57386E819.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse digital media to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.

94EEBC02B6FB45FCA73CB8413A8AA2DB.description: Demonstrate the responsible and ethical use of information and communication technologies by distinguishing between kinds of information that should and should not be publicly shared and describing the consequences of a poor decision.

F45705AB9DE046929C10E7F7A15BD585.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence orally, conveying a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning; ensure alternative or opposing perspectives are addressed; and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and a range of formal and informal tasks.

46BFB0B27E5E458CA5073B566D944821.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

A5EFE628B72C4E84AFCA74C2FDD3E73A.description: Analyze how visual and sound techniques or design (such as special effects, camera angles, and music) carry or influence messages in various media.

232A6648E8864B3D9C448CAAC96C34BA.description: Engage in collaborative discussions about grade-level topics and texts with peers by promoting civil, democratic discussions and decision-making, establishing individual roles, and tracking progress on specific goals; propelling conversations forward by synthesizing comments and ideas of several speakers and responding to diverse perspectives with relevant observations and ideas, resolving contradictions when possible; and determining what additional information is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

31E8E85E670F469C8AC3D695222D9BA5.description: Write by hand or with technology to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

2404BBCB46174AA9A84F32C009329347.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on reframing points to address specific purposes or needs of the audience. (Editing should demonstrate command of grade-level Grammar and Conventions.)

AF0DE020AAD44160AA74BE418AB119F2.description: Produce clear and coherent organizational structures that attend to the norms and conventions of the writing genre, and in which ideas, concepts, and other information build on one another; include formatting and graphics to support the purpose, aid in comprehension, and create a unified whole; and use precise language, content-specific vocabulary, and varied transitions to link major sections of the text, create cohesion and clarify the relationships between and among ideas and concepts.

012E7300F07942A49508C467C2E03829.description: Teachers can include informational and narrative writing at their discretion.

D6087622E26B4C298940BAD6BC9CE54F.description: Teachers can include informational and narrative writing at their discretion.

80AFBAFC4BC84E308A03688E82CCD58A.description: Write arguments that support well-defined points of view that establish the significance of the claim(s) and distinguish those claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims with persuasive evidence and clear reasoning; point out the strengths and limitations of each claim in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, and values; and provide a concluding section that articulates the implications, or the significance, of the argument presented.

EB26BAE8AA3040E1A049D0BB578A0925.description: Develop flexibility in writing by routinely engaging in the production of shorter and longer pieces for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences. This could include, among others, summaries, reflections, descriptions, critiques, letters, and poetry, etc.

227CDD4794B14DED863A6B37160B7EC8.description: Read a series of texts independently, with peers, or with modest support, organized around a variety of conceptually related topics to build knowledge about the world.

A0878A1C072E44AAA5D10788CE2B06A3.description: Deep Reading on Topics to Build Knowledge

F05466D3C4C14492B71D408B26B219F8.description: Conduct brief as well as multi-day research projects to take some action or share findings orally or in writing by formulating multiple interlocking research questions that span the field of inquiry in time and scope; gathering relevant information efficiently from a variety of authoritative sources, as well as from direct observation, interviews, and surveys; making distinctions about the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience, noting any discrepancies among the data; and following a standard approved format (e.g., APA, MLA, Chicago) for citations and bibliographies.

534A1EFA46F245DF9D501543D4DB1128.description: Inquiry Process to Build, Present, and Use Knowledge

F541CF50D0DC4793A53BD61599945864.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and content-specific words and phrases occurring in grade-level reading and content; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression. Use these words in discussions and writing.

B445303EE5964E999A5C37F22E7312A2.description: Analyze the impact of specific word choices on the effectiveness of the message meaning and the tone of the text.

9589B3FDC0AD4BE487E74798599200F8.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations (e.g., aggressive, assertive, forceful, domineering).

977FBFEB6A864FEC9850C43552E54963.description: Analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how FDR explored different ideas regarding freedom in his "Four Freedoms" speech).

58A370B0C35C4F35AA14293E85D279C2.description: Use Greek, Latin, and Norse mythology; and other works often alluded to in American and world literature to understand the meaning of words or phrases (e.g., "narcissistic" from the myth of Narcissus and Echo).

ED1DD40D8C314635916214CA800108C9.description: Determine how words and phrases provide meaning and nuance to texts.

5D148150DB5F472DB960DFB84D16F733.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

8BF402AAEEED49A88AB9B195CBBE9D84.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), print or digital, to find the pronunciation of a grade-level word and determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, its etymology, or its standard usage.

FCF1354520C24C9F873647B4BCB42482.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., symbol, symbolism, symbolic, symbolize).

97A00B1D5205433FB96A0EB1D9EBC7EF.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or portion of text; a word's position or function in a sentence or a sentence within a paragraph) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

2BFB26B0D4604F39AF51CB46AA70E401.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade-level content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

4F9BA9FDFA1B42BB8AE8A363E7E9611C.description: Evaluate the premises and purposes in works of public advocacy.

120EFC1EBA86425A94B701435CE4FE51.description: Analyze the hypotheses, data, analysis, and conclusions in an argument, verifying the data when possible and corroborating or challenging conclusions with other sources of information.

7E2F391065C14211BC2AE9A1562CCC9C.description: Evaluate the effectiveness of the structure(s) and rhetorical devices authors use in their exposition or argument, including whether the structure helps makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

2F79B83C4A3A4BE387767E2AF5FBBE6B.description: Evaluate various explanations of concepts and ideas and determine which explanation best accords with textual evidence, noting discrepancies among sources.

E72CBB56D42A448385083DA611FFCFB3.description: Compare texts that express similar central ideas and analyze in detail how their development and treatment of the topic compares over the course of the two texts; provide accurate summaries of how key events or ideas develop.

D9DF5615322F433891C5E373209B9FFA.description: Use evidence from nonfiction works to demonstrate understanding of grade-level texts.
