A847458A360F4A4BA1DCA5AB345CB32D.description: Evaluate how authors structure texts to distinguish what is directly stated in a text from what is really meant, including satire, sarcasm, irony, and understatement.

6763E595C60F49E298A5AB868CE25F5A.description: Evaluate the choices authors make regarding how to develop and relate several elements of literary texts , including how the characters are introduced and developed and how the action is ordered.

9F2E5C1B120B40FEB74672E7F2C7F3B8.description: Compare the development of a universal theme over the course of two texts, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details in each.

2F7C9CB310E347EC8EA905F11C2FEDE9.description: Use evidence from literature to demonstrate understanding of grade-level texts.

905527B3D65B4D87937874E006CDA37C.description: Regularly engage in a volume of reading, texts independently, with peers, or with modest support related to the topics and themes being studied to build knowledge and vocabulary.

1F6F7300C7D84F28B19001451EC1E0AD.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor.

9A7688855527473187F90950184F52FA.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

35ABDA8094A54555960F9B809E97542C.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

6F2355F5E330469CB7F46F29F04E4236.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.) Constructions include: copying a segment; copying an angle; bisecting a segment; bisecting an angle; constructing perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular bisector of a line segment; and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point not on the line.

B619B0392B834EB981BA666FB64FD8D5.description: Prove theorems about polygons. Theorems include: the measures of interior and exterior angles; apply properties of polygons to the solutions of mathematical and contextual problems.

86A60284409C433D9AACB9A7F661621F.description: Prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.

B3B6ED1920CB4C6591BBBE24725AE871.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent, and conversely prove a triangle is isosceles; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.

1BB52E2E78A44DD99460976E9F92AE7C.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent, and conversely prove lines are parallel; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.

D16AADA13B114F989CF386821CDF9346.description: Prove geometric theorems and, when appropriate, the converse of theorems.

8AA9BCCB90FD40CEAD83FC9BC07E9DB4.description: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.

2A69115F15A64F858B857707AAD60D41.description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

21A1AD7B952F4983857A30C8CD85FA4D.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

97F2D7E9AE7E416E8F9AB8B172C49ABE.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

07CCFA1FA63B4DDEBEA03D55D7B13E2D.description: Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

C4A1BA627D844C3BB8F660C7EFE43A67.description: Draw the transformation (rotation, reflection, or translation) for a given geometric figure.

96DC51A4EDCA474BB00550B96A481169.description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

BC0B9A59068B416C8224E4CA0460C385.description: Describe the rotations and reflections that carry a given figure (rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon) onto itself.

E8280B391FB041EE921B1D3828DCF778.description: Represent transformations in the plane and describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not.

78DACC9081DC479CB8D5DFEE5D12B016.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

844399D5ACE246FCB531FB40D7003B4B.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

71510133C1BB4702AA2A2A1368BF36EB.description: (+) Prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent and use them to solve problems.

AA8078D70DBC451881A313393F19DB06.description: Relate the Pythagorean Theorem to the unit circle to discover the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use the Pythagorean identity to find the value of a trigonometric function (sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ)) given one trigonometric function (sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ)) and the quadrant of the angle.

702C798AD0C440A5B34F3567B6C876AB.description: (+) Use inverse functions to solve trigonometric equations that arise in modeling contexts; evaluate the solutions using technology, and interpret them in terms of the context.

B39858C5402A470AB41BEDC9B62FA9DC.description: (+) Understand that restricting a trigonometric function to a domain on which it is always increasing or always decreasing allows its inverse to be constructed.

09B663352F154C1D8DB805AF97CB0909.description: Model periodic phenomena using trigonometric functions with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

6B51B4DB0980458E94045CB46E042D7F.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions.

85C09253D9304543A296DE30F5756A1C.description: (+) Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions.

C38FE1C5149F49AF94492187A82D97D4.description: (+) Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values of sine, cosine, tangent for π/3, π/4, and π/6, and use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosine, and tangent for π - x, π + x, and 2π - x in terms of their values for x, where x is any real number.

21B4A2EAE07D4E2D82982AB955FA4003.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

0EE4424A2129438690D01911DA1E90F1.description: Use radian measure to solve problems.

FBF7B6638CC84C049E6FE5CF17664A69.description: Demonstrate radian measure as the ratio of the arc length subtended by a central angle to the length of the radius of the unit circle.

C8F75F5FDB664FA8A04C1AD40B1BE6F1.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

A01CF5A215854485B82A706645C37266.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function (of the form f(x) = b<sup>x</sup> + k) in terms of a context.

1B60419915CF42CBB50679E97B98589A.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

E9758F590D0C4EBD8ED4AD98C4120130.description: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to ab<sup>ct</sup> = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the base b is 2,10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

DFF4004E5F5E4A4D85A81DE4AB2E9F75.description: Use graphs and tables to demonstrate that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

243F21C6CFE04893A5AE94A2A80751AC.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (including reading these from a table).

98C19A5FBD4443F59B20AC7027749684.description: Identify situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

9E3B3BBF0106422FA8FEC78B866BD577.description: Identify situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

FA118170DFB94259B503BB446AD1D33A.description: Demonstrate that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

35AE918C31E24170B0729096E4397DBE.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

CCB4F100DD9344CA8E5BE6ECCA8A3760.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

EBFE6DB8710A41A28FF6F635BEF0B10C.description: (+) Produce an invertible function from a non-invertible function by restricting the domain.

E57130BCA73D4A409206AEF38C54AD06.description: (+) Read values of an inverse function from a graph or a table, given that the function has an inverse.

B85FF87B271E49BFBA95FA5B97CB31B5.description: (+) Verify by composition that one function is the inverse of another.

D52B9495C1A644A183A7F6CCEEB357CA.description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. Include linear and simple polynomial, rational, and exponential functions.

B429C81CA4DA4262BBEAB08438ECD2FC.description: Find inverse functions algebraically and graphically.

5BE50F3BEC474E1B947D124B7D25DA01.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, ,f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Include, linear, quadratic, exponential, absolute value, simple rational and radical, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions. Utilize technology to experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

F578C388DB3E482CB6DE8A0C07F6160E.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

31C2D92A96E5437482DC6410287B6962.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

E654446BB07944C0977D526A84802C31.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities. Functions could include linear, exponential, quadratic, simple rational, radical, logarithmic, and trigonometric.

24A1B12FE0D64F8481FC4CEED4AB2BC1.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

756FF0F2494B41E19774F837D41F02F4.description: Given algebraic, numeric and/or graphical representations of functions, recognize the function as polynomial, rational, logarithmic, exponential, or trigonometric.

FFD61B8713374A79BE6BE4801E069517.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

92D4C2777571415E965E5C156D15B630.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions. Apply to financial situations such as identifying appreciation and depreciation rate for the value of a house or car sometime after its initial purchase.

FFD868809119419F80F595F133A3F0EB.description: Use the process of factoring and/or completing the square in quadratic and polynomial functions, where appropriate, to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

EBA01D4062924B07BE1BFB9298217382.description: (+) Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and asymptotes when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

835C4FB130804C7F8F48039FFCFC1A39.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

B64B1445F9B6419980BC9D9579432D33.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

16C30B736C554789AB1B0E721AA59339.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

2979B0167E6A449B81E75C04855BDD01.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

65494B91C9634C729CDB66151D2FF3E0.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maxima and minima; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

0FE02F8BDC5D4004B6EB4A284A5F0BDF.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context. Include linear, quadratic, exponential, rational, polynomial, square root and cube root, trigonometric, and logarithmic functions.

9FE4C8F7479245CB96F14F3FECE90813.description: Demonstrate that a sequence is a functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers.

39B26712A4EA4625BE3971026C49BF69.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

CF88157694DB457F86FF7C5DDE01779B.description: Demonstrate understanding that a function is a correspondence from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) that assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range: If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

211FE87E389C4F3993498EB4969EFE12.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

47CE2F54C91A4685A958409114ACA106.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

9A568236F29745B482C7F657DBEA5FFC.description: Demonstrate understanding that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane. Show that any point on the graph of an equation in two variables is a solution to the equation.

13B4BD9D3774451E9631ACAB71D04165.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

B5B42C3C88524AC2ACB2120BB216A338.description: (+) Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3×3 or greater).

1A15180F28F940CF98E6888F07FD4484.description: (+) Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.

8BFA05C8CCAD4353A8B12B22457B2EC1.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.

2097660D64574D6FB1721ECDFD3B732C.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

ADF41A0B7DA141DFAEA0F93FED635B03.description: Verify that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

F71AF79649C64F3CA815382B2D0ED05F.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49, taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula, and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

1E6B9C18ABD04CFCBA5779F870D293FC.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x - p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

02A393F36F0B46FF927199D3C5CD662D.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

4C8B99BAF1DB459F8C5D67497ECB7479.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable involving absolute value.

ECE7DA7A0DB14AC29283E78902B417EB.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

48D575E22F304F3F9E239AC43C624B1C.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

D39FC0B268CF45CC8C90BC9A83C1709E.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

3461ABBA263F4C6AA754FB12255688CE.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify or refute a solution method.

C316DD8710C544E9850CABB794C38B24.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

30C0C3AF19154C44ADEFF5B119DEED67.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

1C04D29FDAE94B508A9770289B65EE78.description: Represent constraints using systems of equations and/or inequalities and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

2AAE910934D946DC909A63B6E2D0BE48.description: Represent constraints using equations or inequalities and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

5FBD68827CD44ACEB2A282EACB7D00CA.description: Define variables to represent the quantities and write equations to show the relationship.

526BCBFF58234DE3BF4F8953CAF5CB63.description: Interpret the relationship between two or more quantities.

8CECEABD3B7A4F97A3CBAE2CA96DC912.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

BD6B79C2761C453BB1B53359F8EB6693.description: (+) Demonstrate understanding that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

4BBB5B76E9D9480ABDB7223C85EF06A1.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

FC8E10D540F34BADBE225929FD96A573.description: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)<sup>n</sup> in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined, for example, by Pascal's Triangle.

4DD36CAD9D2242B093EDB2899E6A7CB4.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.

434D2E58B00E4189AABFDED601E94674.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

A06FDC4A7B8141E6A11165F174EE8E80.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

C58C5BE272C64196B633C9B0805C0357.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x - a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x - a) is a factor of p(x).

8BFA2E94BC994F2083CDAB9A007C3A4F.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

5436D80ADC1741A992E15450F03BF4F4.description: Factor and/or expand polynomial expressions, identify and combine like terms, and apply the distributive property.

858BEF8DBE794ACB88B7F595096FF862.description: Perform operations on polynomial expressions (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and compare the system of polynomials to the system of integers when performing operations.

1800D1BE14DE4FDF949D5280FB28FA39.description: Demonstrate understanding that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers; namely, they are closed under certain operations.

6237131F3A5B4634AF1D40AD5D8E77CF.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

F25010F028EB4AA38E88BF9F1420C189.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1) and use the formula to solve problems.

39D1F0F5D3F94063966DDBBF9286E02C.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.

4D65108B3AAA415582EABFB7A9EE2EBE.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

78029C94A98E4D8B9222E55E430CBF7B.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

76A8D16751DC49F8A478206A6DA9A867.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

884790830CA14FC787A49B8BD244A83F.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

1B5B672375B047FD9D766A92BEC483E7.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

9D8EF5A7D84949629769674202E7FAD9.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

5C470A9253AF4852B548EDF62E147362.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

707E9307CF3C46B385577333D585A023.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

C5510DBC81D64B1F970F0652A472A778.description: Interpret the structure of linear, quadratic, exponential, polynomial, and rational expressions.

The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

8B112FC964F54CBB8ACC3D4635330D0D.description: (+) Demonstrate understanding that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

8AC89BC0675C4D6F85E1C8BB878868A2.description: (+) Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.

4DAC2816C64449E7A5166C9CC1003CD9.description: (+) Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, e.g., as when all of the payoffs in a game are doubled.

ED6113BE82464A3FA12E8C14354267D5.description: (+) Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network.

86D55A3068FA490CA5F27FC7DA39926F.description: (+) Multiply a vector by a scalar.

935D029A6A674D8D8BB2835F7487EE6E.description: (+) Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.
